title: Design: database providers, access levels and vault-based credentials for connection storage
author: SmearODeer
body_snippet:
Follow-up to #3249, as discussed there. This issue is for agreeing on a design before anyone writes code. Everything below is a proposal; please correct or reject any part of it.

## Goal (from #3249)

- Admins define named database servers ("providers"), for example DEV-TEST and PROD.
- No passwords are stored in profiles or settings, only a reference to a secret in a vault.
- Users without a vault get a basic local store, encrypted for the machine (section 2 proposes per user instead).

## Access model: scopes and roles

Part of the database providers design (#3632), and follows the RBAC discussion in #3249, #3653 and #3655.

### Summary
- Connections are split into **scopes**.
- Each person's Windows login decides which scopes they see and what they may do in each one.
- mRemoteNG passes that login through to the database, and **the database enforces the rules**. This holds even when someone opens the database with another tool.

## Setup tool: building the enterprise database

Follows the access model above. That model needs a database with tables, row-level security, stored procedures and group logins. This section describes the tool that builds it. It is written so that an enterprise can approve it under its security and audit rules: least privilege, segregation of duties, a review before any change, and a record of what was done.
